column2: How much notice must a principal normally give the FCA before appointing a new representative?
column7: The principal must notify the FCA at least 30 days before the appointment takes effect. The notice period runs before the representative starts work.

column2: A principal's annual review identifies serious failings at an appointed representative. Who must consider the findings?
column7: The FCA requires the principal to escalate significant issues from its review for consideration by its own governing body.

column2: A retail investment adviser logs 35 CPD hours, including 16 structured hours. How many more structured hours are needed?
column7: The FCA specifies a minimum of 21 structured hours within the annual 35. Subtracting the 16 already completed leaves five.

column2: Who issues a retail investment adviser's annual Statement of Professional Standing?
column7: An accredited body verifies that the adviser meets the professional standards and issues the statement. The employer remains responsible for assessing the adviser's competence.

column2: A nominee holds all a company's shares for one individual. Whose identity matters for beneficial ownership checks?
column7: Customer checks look through a nominee to the individual who ultimately owns or controls the company. Authority to sign for the company is a different test.

column2: A client's new passport conflicts with identity details on file. Which check must the firm repeat?
column7: Doubt about the identification evidence triggers fresh due diligence to establish who the customer is. An enquiry into the origin of wealth answers a different question.

column2: Under its internal reporting procedure, whom should an adviser's first money laundering disclosure reach?
column7: The nominated officer receives internal disclosures from staff and decides whether to report the suspicion to the National Crime Agency.

column2: Who must approve a new business relationship with a foreign politically exposed person?
column7: Enhanced due diligence for a politically exposed person includes senior approval, enquiries about wealth and funds, and closer monitoring.

column2: A customer objects to marketing but keeps their account. Which record helps the firm screen future mailing lists?
column7: The firm can retain a limited record of the objection to exclude the customer from promotional contact. A past consent record does not override a later objection.

column2: A client phones to correct an inaccurate employer entry. How should the firm classify the call?
column7: A person can ask for inaccurate personal data to be corrected by telephone. A request for access would seek a copy of the information.

column2: Eight weeks after complaining about investment advice, a customer still has no reply. Where can they take it?
column7: The ordinary eight-week period for the business to address this kind of complaint has expired. The consumer can now refer it to the ombudsman without a final response.

column2: An investor disagrees with a complaint investigator's assessment. Who can make a final decision within the Financial Ombudsman Service?
column7: Either side can request a decision from an ombudsman after the initial assessment. The investigator's view does not bind the parties.

column2: A failed broker lost £3,000 of Jo's custody assets. A market fall cost Jo £2,000. Which loss might FSCS cover?
column7: The custody shortfall may qualify if the claim meets FSCS conditions. The separate fall in market prices is ordinary investment performance.

column2: A final salary scheme's sponsor becomes insolvent. What does the PPF valuation establish?
column6: Tax due on the sponsor's estate
column7: The valuation tests whether the scheme's assets can secure benefits at the PPF level. An insolvent sponsor alone does not settle whether the scheme transfers.

column2: During a PPF assessment, whom should members contact about the pension their scheme is paying?
column7: The trustees remain the point of contact for member benefits during assessment. The scheme has not yet transferred to the PPF.

column2: Which complaint falls within the Pensions Ombudsman's remit?
column4: Advice to buy a personal pension
column7: Unreasonable delay by occupational scheme trustees concerns administration. State Pension matters and complaints about sales fall outside this ombudsman's remit.

column2: A 58-year-old wants impartial guidance on drawing a defined contribution pot. Which service provides it?
column7: Pension Wise, offered through MoneyHelper, explains ways to take a defined contribution pension and how they are generally taxed.

column2: An investor complains on 2 March and receives a final response on 23 March. What is the earliest referral date?
column7: The investor can refer the complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service on receiving the firm's final response. Waiting eight weeks is unnecessary once the firm has answered.

column2: A nominated officer decides a staff disclosure warrants an external suspicious activity report. Where should it go?
column7: The nominated officer considers the internal disclosure and submits any required suspicious activity report to the National Crime Agency.

column2: A firm becomes aware of a reportable UK GDPR breach. Where feasible, when must it notify the ICO?
column7: For a breach that must be reported, the usual deadline runs for 72 hours from awareness. The firm should not wait until its investigation is complete to make the initial notification.

column2: A professional client needs more investor protection for an unfamiliar transaction. What may it request?
column7: Firms must allow professional clients to request a category offering greater protection. Making the request does not oblige the firm to grant it.

column2: A firm recommends only funds run by its parent company. How should it describe its investment advice?
column7: Limiting recommendations to the corporate group's own products rules out independent advice. Selecting a product for the individual is still advice.

column2: When should a firm tell a new client whether its investment advice is independent or restricted?
column7: The client needs to know the scope of the service before receiving advice. Stating it on a later invoice would be too late.

column2: Which statement turns an insurance sales conversation into a personal recommendation?
column3: This policy best suits your needs
column4: This policy has a compulsory excess
column7: Identifying a particular policy as suitable for the customer goes beyond describing features or availability. The customer is being steered towards a contract on personal grounds.

column2: A client asks an adviser to arrange a transaction contrary to the recommendation already given. Which description applies?
column7: The client has received advice and wants the firm to carry out a different transaction. Receiving and rejecting advice differs from placing an order without advice.

column2: An adviser recommends keeping a bond. Which instruction best records an insistent client's acknowledgement?
column3: I want to sell despite your advice to keep it
column4: I want you to quote the cost of selling it
column5: I want to check the risks before I sell it
column6: I want advice on when to sell the bond
column7: The acknowledgement should establish that the client chooses to proceed contrary to the recommendation. A request for a quotation or more advice leaves that decision open.

column2: A retail investment adviser sets a tariff. Which factor can justify a higher fee for one client's advice?
column3: More work on the client's case
column4: Higher margin on the chosen fund
column6: Higher bonus at a sales threshold
column7: The charging structure should reflect the service provided. The issuer's own margin or sales incentives do not measure the work done for the client.

column2: An adviser and investor agree a fee. Which payment arrangement is permitted?
column4: Provider commission rebated to the client
column5: Volume bonus credited against the fee
column7: A provider may facilitate the agreed adviser charge by deducting it from the investment. Rebating commission does not make accepting it permissible for new retail investment advice.

column2: A firm takes an annual advice fee on a new lump-sum investment. What should the client have agreed?
column7: An ongoing adviser charge on this investment requires an agreed ongoing service. A provider's annual fund charge pays for something different.

column2: A client likes volatile investments but relies on this money for rent. Which risk measure concerns the adviser?
column7: Losses could affect the client's ability to meet essential costs. A willingness to take risk does not establish the financial ability to sustain it.

column2: Which detail helps an adviser assess a client's experience with a proposed investment?
column7: Past transactions in comparable products show what the client has encountered. Borrowings and withdrawal targets inform different parts of the suitability assessment.

column2: A client withholds facts the firm needs to assess investment suitability. What must the firm withhold?
column7: Without the necessary client information the firm cannot recommend a particular investment. Supplying factual information does not itself amount to a personal recommendation.

column2: Which entry belongs under regular financial commitments in an investment fact-find?
column6: Net proceeds from a house sale
column7: Recurring payments on debts are commitments that reduce income available for investment. Asset values and receipts are recorded elsewhere.

column2: Which finding supports a MiFID adviser's recommendation to switch investments?
column3: Expected benefits outweigh the costs of switching
column4: Replacement fund meets the original investment objective
column5: Replacement fund offers a wider investment mandate
column6: Projected return matches the existing fund's return
column7: The adviser must compare the costs and benefits of the change and be able to demonstrate that the benefits outweigh the costs. Meeting the original objective alone leaves the case for switching unresolved.

column2: An adviser recommends a bond with an investment service. Each suits Priya separately. What remains to establish?
column3: Whether using them together suits Priya
column4: Whether Priya could buy them separately
column5: Whether Priya understands the separate fees
column6: Whether Priya is experienced with each
column7: Suitability of a bundled recommendation depends on how the combination works for the client. Availability, charges and experience can inform the advice without establishing that the package suits her.

column2: Lee fits a model portfolio's target market. Which comparison establishes the outstanding suitability judgement?
column3: Lee's own objectives against the strategy
column4: Lee's risk score against the entry threshold
column5: Lee's assets against the minimum holding
column6: Lee's age against the intended age range
column7: Checking eligibility can show that Lee falls within the intended market. The adviser must still judge whether the proposal fits his individual needs, objectives and financial circumstances.

column2: A pension switch could give up a guaranteed income. Which comparison addresses that loss?
column7: The adviser must establish the features a replacement would remove as well as those it would add. Comparing fund yields alone would miss the guarantee.

column2: An adviser researches a fund's strategy, risks and benefits. What further subject does product due diligence cover?
column7: Research includes the provider and whether it is appropriate to entrust assets to it. A client's tax position and experience belong in the separate client assessment.

column2: A client retires and replaces a salary with pension drawdown. Which part of the fact-find needs revising on those facts?
column7: The change directly affects how income is funded. An adviser aware of the retirement cannot rely on a salary figure from the earlier fact-find.

column2: A firm promises periodic MiFID suitability assessments. What is the longest usual interval between them?
column7: An agreed periodic assessment must take place at least annually. The client and the investments may justify a shorter interval.

column2: A firm agrees to reassess a client's MiFID investments periodically. Which communication detail must it disclose?
column4: How to give instructions for each trade
column5: How the custodian will report income
column6: How the provider will announce dividends
column7: For a periodic suitability assessment the firm discloses how it will communicate updated advice. Custody statements and dividend notices concern separate services.

column2: What standard cancellation period usually applies when a retail client joins a personal pension scheme?
column7: COBS ordinarily gives someone joining a personal pension 30 calendar days to cancel. The shorter period applies to some other contracts.

column2: Who must give or check advice on moving final salary rights into a flexible retirement pot?
column7: Defined benefit transfer advice requires specialist involvement. The scheme administrator processes the transfer but does not replace the specialist's advice check.

column2: A client reports the recent death of her partner. Under which FCA vulnerability driver does bereavement itself fall?
column7: The FCA classifies bereavement as a life event. It can also affect someone's health or resilience, so the firm should ask what support the individual needs.
